idiom_name: enum with data-carrying variants + an explicit children() method
implementation_notes: Rust expresses the heterogeneous node set as one enum whose variants carry node-specific data, wrapped in a struct that adds shared fields (span, id); the normalized child accessor is an explicit children() returning references, implemented by one match arm per variant, so generic passes recurse over it while match exhaustiveness (checked by the compiler) covers per-node dispatch. Box, Rc or arena indices supply the indirection recursive variants need. The syn crate is the library reference at scale: heterogeneous node structs plus generated Visit traits for traversal. A visitor trait is worth adding when many passes live in separate modules; otherwise children() plus match is the idiom.
pitfalls: Returning Vec<&Expr> allocates for every node on every walk; return an iterator or a small-vector type for hot passes.
Recursive variants must indirect through Box/Rc or an arena index: a variant holding a child by value makes the type infinitely sized and fails to compile.
Borrow rules make in-place rewriting awkward - holding &self while mutating children does not compile; rewriters need an arena/index scheme or an owned split before mutation.
